projects.title: A Voice for Fine Wine
projects.summary: A bilingual content system for the oldest fine-wine house in America — one voice across Instagram and RedNote, in two languages, without sounding translated.

blocks.heading: The problem
blocks.body:
Fine wine copy defaults to two failure modes: auction-catalogue dryness, or the kind of florid tasting-note prose nobody under fifty reads. Acker needed to sound like a two-hundred-year-old house that still goes to dinner.

And it needed to work twice — English on Instagram, Chinese on RedNote — where a straight translation reads as a straight translation.

blocks.caption: Instagram grid — one voice, three post shapes

blocks.text: Say the wine, say why it matters, stop.
blocks.attribution: The rule the whole system runs on

blocks.caption: RedNote posts are written natively, not translated

projects.title: The Tool Suite
projects.summary: A suite of hand-built, single-file web tools that let a marketing team across nine cities produce on-brand collateral without a designer in the room.

blocks.heading: The problem
blocks.body:
Nine cities, one brand, and a marketing team that needed a one-pager by Thursday. Every request routed through a designer, so every request waited.

The fix was not a template library. It was a set of tools that make the brand the path of least resistance.

blocks.caption: One-Pager Builder — brand rules enforced by the tool, not by review

projects.title: 醫卓所 — A Cast of Characters
projects.summary: A 3D character canon and animated content system built to make clinical expertise feel human — locked scale, locked look, infinitely extendable.

blocks.heading: Locked canon
blocks.body:
The hard part of a character system is not the first character. It's the fortieth, made eight months later by someone else, still looking like it belongs.

So the canon locks first: proportion, scale relationships, material response, camera language. Everything after that is assembly.

projects.title: Seven Scenes
projects.summary: A scroll-driven cinematic where the page scrub drives a single continuous camera through seven worlds — each one rebuilt from a real project.

blocks.caption: Seven Scenes — continuous camera, no cuts

blocks.heading: One camera, no cuts
blocks.body:
Scroll position drives video currentTime. The camera flies out of one world and into the next without a cut, so the whole portfolio reads as a single take.

The constraint is what makes it: if you can't cut, every transition has to be designed.

projects.title: Landing in Tokyo
projects.summary: Market-entry collateral for two new Tokyo centres — drawn network maps, bilingual one-pagers, and a launch page built in a week.

blocks.heading: One week
blocks.body: Two centres, a launch date that had already been announced, and no photography yet. The drawn network map became the hero because it was the one asset that didn't depend on a shoot.

projects.title: Keeping the Songs
projects.summary: Identity and film support for a London association making the case to Arts Council England that a four-hundred-year-old art form still has an audience.

blocks.heading: The case
blocks.body: Funding bodies do not respond to heritage claims. They respond to evidence of an audience. The work had to show a living art form, not an archive.
